name: CRB-65 Score

citations.text: Lim WS, van der Eerden MM, Laing R, et al. Defining community acquired pneumonia severity on presentation to hospital: an international derivation and validation study. Thorax. 2003;58(5):377-382.

validated_population: Adults with community-acquired pneumonia presenting to hospital. CRB-65 is the version without a blood test, intended for community settings.
self_report_note: The score was validated in people already diagnosed with pneumonia. Here it is used to judge how urgently to be seen. Breathing rate and blood pressure need to be measured.
license_note: Published clinical score; not a copyrighted instrument. Question wording is original to OLA BOT.

red_flags.question: If you have a home pulse oximeter, is your oxygen level below 92%?
Are you coughing up more than a teaspoon of blood?
red_flags.help: Coughing up blood needs prompt evaluation.

items.question: Is there any new confusion (not knowing the date, place, or people who are normally familiar)?
items.help: Ask a family member if unsure.

items.question: Count your breaths for 30 seconds while resting, then double it. Is it 30 or more breaths per minute?
items.help: One breath = one rise and fall of the chest. Have someone else count if possible.

items.question: If you can measure your blood pressure: is the top number below 90, or the bottom number 60 or lower?
items.help: Choose Not sure if you have no blood pressure monitor.
items.trace_label: B: Blood pressure <90 systolic or ≤60 diastolic

scoring.threshold_text: 0 = low risk; 1–2 = intermediate risk; 3–4 = high risk.

low.label: Low risk
low.interpretation: In the validation study, people with a CRB-65 score of 0 had a low risk of death (about 1 in 100). Home treatment is usually possible if pneumonia is confirmed.
low.recommendation: See a clinician to check whether you have pneumonia or a simpler chest infection.

care.where_detail: Telehealth or primary care visit; urgent care if you cannot be seen within 48 hours.
ed_redirect: Lips or face turning blue or gray: call 911
Oxygen below 92% or severe shortness of breath
self_care: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen as labeled for fever.

intermediate.label: Intermediate risk
intermediate.interpretation: Your score is in the intermediate range. The study authors advised clinical assessment to decide between home and hospital care.
intermediate.recommendation: Get an in-person exam today, which may include a chest X-ray.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic with X-ray, or emergency department if you are 65 or older and feel very unwell.
ed_redirect: Lips or face turning blue or gray: call 911
Oxygen below 92% or severe shortness of breath

high.label: High risk
high.interpretation: Your score is in the high range. People with scores of 3 or 4 usually need hospital care.
high.recommendation: Go to an emergency department now.

care.where_detail: Hospital emergency department. Call 911 if you are too short of breath to travel safely.
ed_redirect: Lips or face turning blue or gray: call 911
Oxygen below 92% or severe shortness of breath
